outcome: tooth wear (assessed by Smith and Knight Tooth Wear Index)
cohort: The study included 129 children and adolescents aged 3-7 years (primary dentition) and 10-17 years (permanent dentition), consisting of 70 asthmatic patients receiving inhaled therapy and 59 healthy controls.
finding: Asthmatic patients receiving inhaled therapy, especially with combination regimens and DPIs, had significantly more tooth wear compared to healthy controls, with wear correlating with higher ICS doses and longer treatment duration.
